title: Python: first-party root discovery misses a nested source root (<subproject>/python); glyph fails closed on the whole repository
description: Discovered during GCLI-174 scored run (DEC-303 (a109) item 2). On the pydantic checkout at 6449f80d, shipped glyph exited 7: python: 283 first-party package roots did not resolve to a source root; first: PydanticUndefined at pydantic-core/python/pydantic_core/core_schema.py:24 names pydantic_core. pydantic vendors pydantic-core at pydantic-core/python/pydantic_core, with its project marker at pydantic-core/pyproject.toml. First-party root discovery does not treat a nested source root such as <subproject>/python as a source root, so every pydantic_core import fails closed and the whole repository is indeterminate (no index, no answer). This is a product defect: glyph refuses to index a repository it should analyze. Build and prove on fixtures only; the pydantic blind-sample checkout is spent held-out material and is not read for design (DEC-303 (a36) item 8; (a109) item 2). No hold.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fixture repository with a vendored subproject at <sub>/python/<pkg> and a project marker at <sub>/ builds a glyph index with exit 0 and resolves imports of <pkg> in-repo, where the frozen head exits 7 today.
A fixture with a nested source root whose package is genuinely absent still exits 7 with a named first-party root trigger, so the fix does not turn an indeterminate into a silent answer.
The pydantic 6449f80d shape (a vendored pydantic-core at pydantic-core/python/pydantic_core) is reduced to a fixture and proved without reading any spent blind-sample checkout (DEC-303 (a36) item 8).
No blind-sample checkout is read and no spent sample is used to build or prove the fix.
